detail.longDescription: I have a SQL Server Always On Availability Group with one primary replica and one readable secondary replica. I want my Node.js application to send read-only connections to the secondary replica. I am using the mssql package and the Availability Group listener in the connection configuration: const sql = require('mssql'); const config = { server: 'my-ag-listener', database: 'my_database', user: process.env.DB_USER, password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD, options: { encrypt: true, trustServerCertificate: true, applicationIntent: 'ReadOnly' } }; The connection succeeds, but when I execute: const pool = await sql.connect(config); const result = await pool.request().query(` SELECT @@SERVERNAME AS server_name; `); the result shows the name of the primary SQL Server instance instead of the readable secondary replica. The same Availability Group is configured with a read-only routing URL and a read-only routing list, and I can verify the expected routing when connecting with a client that supports ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly . Does node-mssql support SQL Server Always On read-only routing through applicationIntent: 'ReadOnly' ? If it does, what is the correct connection configuration for mssql to allow SQL Server to perform the read-only routing?
